newsitem.title: USA: Gillette, Duracell shares cool off.
newsitem.headline: Gillette, Duracell shares cool off.

text.p: Gillette Co and Duracell International Inc shares cooled off Monday after their $7 billion merger pact drew raves from investors last week, stoking sharp gains in extremely active trade.
Traders and arbitrageurs agreed the price declines are coming from sellers locking in these gains, and not from a change in the market's positive view of the transaction.
In midafternoon trade, Gillette was off 3/4 to 69-5/8, up from an intraday low of 68-7/8, and Duracell gave back one to 61-3/4, above the 60-7/8 intraday low.

"It was a very rapid run-up Friday," said Salomon Bros analyst Diana Temple. "I would have expected a couple of points, but (Gillette) was up five. After a run-up like that, it's not surprising" for the stocks to fall back.
Duracell finished last week at 62-3/4 up from 49-1/8, the price before the deal was announced Thursday morning, while Gillette leaped to 70-3/8 from 66 over the two sessions.
Temple characterized an investors conference held earlier Monday between Gillette CEO Alfred Zeien, Duracell chief Charles Perrin and Merrill Lynch & Co as "being very upbeat."
An arbitrageur described the tone of the call "bullish," similar to the Thursday conference call that detailed the transaction.

A second arbitrageur said it was unlikley that investors found negative details in the full agreement filed with the U.S. Securites and Exchange Commission this morning, calling the document "one of the cleanest I've ever seen."
